public_rationale: Zitron says Opus 4.7 'appears to' perform worse and consume more tokens. Under the supplied rules, that tentative wording cannot be scored as a firm benchmark claim. Anthropic documents a tokenizer change that can increase input-token counts, but this does not settle the broader tentative assessment.
limitations: This disposition neither endorses nor rejects the reported user experiences.
The tokenization evidence concerns input encoding, not total tokens required for equivalent successful work.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Opus 4.7 appears to perform worse than its predecessor and to consume more tokens.

statement.excerpt: Things only got worse with last week’s launch of Opus 4.7, which appears to have worse performance and burn more tokens.

from_speaker: appears to have worse performance and burn more tokens
our_interpretation: The comparison is with Opus 4.6, which the preceding passage discusses.
The qualification 'appears to' applies to both performance and token consumption. It expresses a tentative assessment, not a firm comparative result.
Benchmark results and token measurements can inform the assessment, but cannot supply a commitment the speaker did not make.
criteria.support_condition: No binary support condition is assigned to this tentative assertion. Treating measured regression as its required meaning would strengthen the speaker's wording.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No binary contradiction condition is assigned. Better benchmark performance would not establish that the reported appearance of regression was false.
